# Researching and ingesting wiki evidence

Choose the mode explicitly from the request. An unspecified request to use this
role is not permission to process the whole backlog; clarify the intended task.
Treat `` as the request when the host has not substituted it.

- **Discover sources on a topic:** read [discovery](references/discover.md),
  [access](../wiki-maintainer/references/access.md),
  [evidence](../wiki-maintainer/references/evidence.md), and
  [efficacy](../wiki-maintainer/references/efficacy.md). Research perspectives
  return candidates without writing. Use the capture route only within the
  requested scope; a request for candidates alone remains read-only.
- **Capture named URLs or saved web pages:** read [named capture](references/capture.md)
  and [access](../wiki-maintainer/references/access.md). Skip broad topic research;
  preserve deduplication, declines and capture checks.
- **Capture a named format or service:** read its complete route:
  [PDF](references/clip-pdf.md), [Word](references/clip-docx.md),
  [PowerPoint](references/clip-pptx.md), [spreadsheets](references/clip-xlsx.md),
  [GitHub repository](references/clip-gh.md), or
  [Confluence](references/clip-confluence.md). These routes include prerequisite
  checks; missing converters or authentication never justify fabricated evidence.
- **Ingest named existing clippings:** read [ingestion](references/ingest.md),
  [access](../wiki-maintainer/references/access.md), and
  [evidence](../wiki-maintainer/references/evidence.md). Use the exact source set;
  do not rediscover it or silently expand to the global backlog.
- **Process new or un-ingested clippings without a filename:** read
  [ingestion](references/ingest.md) and the
  [hash-join backlog contract](../wiki-maintainer/references/maintenance.md).
  Determine eligibility before writing. Preserve already summarized sources and
  reject restricted evidence as support. If nothing eligible is pending, report
  that without opening an operation, logging, committing or refreshing indexes.

Capture-only requests create evidence, never derived source or concept pages.
Ingestion needs authorization for that source set; an explicitly requested full
research-and-ingest flow already provides it. Only capture tools write raw
artifacts, and agents never edit their bodies. Read
[evidence](../wiki-maintainer/references/evidence.md) before assessing fidelity,
quoting or synthesizing; preserve restrictions and platform-specific sections.

Before the first authorized mutation, read
[operation completion](../wiki-maintainer/references/operations.md). Finish the
scoped validation, log, commit, sync and remote verification unless publication
is held. Reuse an enclosing operation when it owns the work; preserve other
writers' edits. For concept reuse and relationship changes read
[efficacy](../wiki-maintainer/references/efficacy.md).

5	# Clipping a PDF into the wiki
6	
7	The HTML clipper (`clip.mjs` → Defuddle) handles **HTML** pages only; a
8	PDF URL or local paper extracts as thin content and is skipped. This reference covers the
9	PDF path. **The canonical stored artifact is the extracted Markdown, never the
10	binary PDF** — that keeps the vault greppable, diffable, and answerable, and makes
11	`[[note]]` provenance resolve to a real Markdown clipping rather than to an opaque
12	attachment.
13	
14	> Storing the `.md` is the rule for *new* clippings. It does **not** mean deleting
15	> PDFs that already live in `raw/` and are cited as `[[file.pdf]]` — Obsidian
16	> resolves those attachment links, and `health.mjs` now recognizes them too, so
17	> historical PDF attachments are healthy as-is. Only convert an existing PDF on
18	> explicit request.
19	
20	## How it works
21	
22	`clip-pdf.mjs` extracts text with **`pdftotext`** — either the **Xpdf** or the
23	**poppler** build, probed at runtime, with Xpdf preferred because only it provides
24	the `-table` mode that reads a tabular PDF without destroying its rows (invoked via Node's
25	`execFileSync`, which resolves the Windows `.exe` correctly — do **not** shell out
26	to `pdftotext` from a Bash tool per the PATHEXT hazard), then writes
27	`raw/clippings/<slug>.md` with the standard clipping frontmatter (`source`,
28	`created`, `tags:[clippings]`, `quality`, `source-hash`). It skips duplicates and
29	prior declines, and records a decline for **thin** extractions (scanned/image PDFs
30	that need OCR) so they are not retried blindly.
31	
32	Extraction is tuned for academic PDFs:
33	- **UTF-8 output (`-enc UTF-8`).** pdftotext defaults to Latin-1 on some builds;
34	  Node then decodes those bytes as UTF-8 and turns every accent/bullet/© into `�`
35	  ("Béthune" → "B�thune"). Forcing UTF-8 fixes that at the source — no OCR needed
36	  for accented text.
37	- **Reading mode chosen per document, not globally.** `pdftotext` has two
38	  incompatible-by-design modes and the right one depends on the layout:
39	  - *Reading-order* (default) follows the text stream column-by-column. Correct for a
40	    **two-column paper** — each column reads top-to-bottom and hyphenated breaks are
41	    joined, so prose comes out quotable.
42	  - *Aligned* (`-table`) preserves horizontal position, so a row's cells stay on one
43	    output line. Correct for a **table**; it interleaves a two-column paper.
44	
45	  Applied globally, either one is wrong for half of all documents. Reading-order mode
46	  on a **table** emits it column-block-wise — the whole key column, then the whole
47	  value column — so every row's key is detached from its value and the pairing is
48	  unrecoverable from the output. So the clipper samples the first pages both ways and
49	  routes on the result: if short standalone lines get *re-attached* as the leading
50	  token of a longer line in aligned mode, the document is tabular.
51	- **A tabular clipping never claims plain `high` fidelity.** Recovered rows are stamped
52	  `extraction: table-aware` + **`fidelity: tabular`** — the pairings were *reconstructed
53	  from horizontal position*, not read off a structured source, so confirm a pairing
54	  before quoting it as verbatim.
55	- **`-table` is an Xpdf feature; poppler does not have it.** When the installed
56	  `pdftotext` cannot align a document that was detected as tabular, the clipper
57	  **warns on stderr and stamps `extraction: table-flattened` + `fidelity: degraded`**
58	  rather than writing a clean-looking clipping whose rows are silently mispaired.
59	  Install the [Xpdf command-line tools](https://www.xpdfreader.com/download.html) and
60	  re-clip to recover the rows. `-layout` is deliberately **not** used as a fallback:
61	  it can stack consecutive keys into a column while their values drift.
62	- **OCR fallback (Tesseract).** For a **scanned/image PDF** (no text layer) the
63	  clipper automatically rasterizes pages with `pdftoppm` and recognizes them with
64	  **Tesseract** — previously these were just declined. Pass **`--ocr`** to force
65	  the OCR path on any PDF whose embedded-font layer is broken beyond what UTF-8
66	  fixes (e.g. a math-symbol font with no Unicode mapping). OCR is slower and has
67	  its own error modes (superscripts, math), so it is a fallback, not the default;
68	  OCR'd clippings are tagged `extraction: ocr` in frontmatter. Optional
69	  `--ocr-lang=<code>` (default `eng`).
70	- **Running headers/footers stripped.** The repeated title line and page-number
71	  footer at each page boundary are detected (a boundary line recurring on ≥ half
72	  the pages, with digits masked so `5-70`/`5-71` collapse) and removed — otherwise
73	  they stitch into the middle of an otherwise-verbatim quote.
74	- **Fidelity flag.** Math/symbol fonts (especially in older PDFs) extract lossily —
75	  `−`→`?`, `‖`→`jj`, superscripts flatten. This **cannot** be fixed without OCR, so
76	  it is *flagged*: when mangling is detected, the frontmatter gets
77	  **`fidelity: degraded`**. Clean captures omit the field. The full set of values a
78	  clipping can carry is: *(absent)* = high, **`tabular`** = rows reconstructed from
79	  layout, **`ocr`** = the text was recognised from page images, **`degraded`** = do
80	  not trust verbatim spans. Precedence is `degraded` over `ocr` over `tabular`: wrong
81	  characters are the worse defect, and recognised text with plausible characters is
82	  worse than a reconstructed pairing because nothing in the characters can show what
83	  the engine got wrong.
84	- **An OCR clipping never claims plain `high` fidelity.** Recognition errors produce
85	  well-formed words (`hrst` for `first`), so no check on the text can find them; the
86	  clipper declares the floor instead, `extraction: ocr` + **`fidelity: ocr`**, whether
87	  OCR was forced with `--ocr` or ran as the automatic fallback. A clean OCR pass is
88	  stamped the same as a poor one: the value says *unverified*, not *bad*. Clippings
89	  made before the floor existed carry `extraction: ocr` and no grade;
90	  `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/refresh-fidelity.mjs" --ocr-floor` lists them
91	  (dry run) and, with `--apply`, sets the floor. `refresh-fidelity.mjs` never clears an OCR flag, because
92	  re-reading the characters would call it healthy.
93	- **A text layer that drops or shifts letters is `degraded`.** A broken font map can leave only valid letters: some vanish, the whole alphabet shifts, or one letter stands for another. No other check sees it, because the characters are all letters. No Latin-script text lacks an `a` or a `t`, in any language, so a text of at least 5,000 letters whose share of one of fourteen common letters is far below every language's share is stamped `degraded` and sent to OCR. A shorter text, and a text that is not mostly Latin script, are not judged. Clippings made before this check are not re-graded for you: `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/refresh-fidelity.mjs" --inventory` lists the unmarked ones that now look broken, and only lists.
94	- **Re-assessment cannot clear a table flag.** `refresh-fidelity.mjs` re-derives
95	  fidelity from the stored text and drops flags that no longer hold, but a
96	  table-derived flag has no basis in the characters (a flattened table reads as
97	  clean prose), so clippings carrying `extraction: table-aware` or `table-flattened`
98	  are preserved rather than cleared.
99	
100	## Steps
101	
102	1. **Preflight** (once): `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/clip-pdf.mjs" --doctor`. It probes every
103	   external tool and prints what each missing one costs you; it is silent-and-OK only
104	   when all four are present. The clipper also prints this banner on **every** run
105	   when something is missing, so a degraded toolchain cannot go unnoticed. A missing
106	   `pdftotext` is fatal and the clipper exits — do not fabricate content. The rest are
107	   degradations: no `-table` loses table row pairings, and no `pdftoppm`/`tesseract`
108	   means scanned PDFs cannot be read at all.
109	2. **Clip** (this is the only writer to `raw/`):
110	   `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/clip-pdf.mjs" "<path/to/file.pdf>" --source="<canonical-url-if-any>" --quality=<tier> --topic="<topic>"`
111	   - `--source` is the citable origin (the paper's DOI/URL). Omit for a purely
112	     local PDF and the file path is recorded as the source.
113	   - **`--topic` whenever this clip belongs to a research run** — pass the topic
114	     string researcher discovery was given, identical across every clip in the run.
115	     It is what lets maintainer triage group the run's leftovers together. **Topic is
116	     recorded going forward only: there is no tool that can retro-fit it**, so a
117	     clip made without it is an *Unattributed* triage row permanently. Omit it
118	     only for a one-off clip with no research run behind it — an invented topic
119	     is worse than none, because it files the row under a heading the user has
120	     already worked through.
121	   - `--figures[=auto|all|3,5-7]` also renders figure pages (see **Preserving figures**).
122	     Pass it whenever the PDF's value is in graphs, diagrams or photos.
123	   - `--mode=auto|reading-order|table` overrides the reading-mode detector for a
124	     document it gets wrong. See **Overriding the reading mode** below.
125	   - A `thin` result means the PDF is scanned/encrypted and OCR also failed — a
126	     decline is recorded. An `ocr-unavailable` result means the OCR toolchain is
127	     missing, so **nothing was learned about the PDF** — no decline is recorded;
128	     install the tools and re-clip. Never invent the text either way.
129	3. **Verify** the clipping landed: read `raw/clippings/<slug>.md` and sanity-check
130	   that the extracted text is real prose, not garbled ligatures. `pdftotext`
131	   output is plain text — light and lossy on tables/figures.
132	4. **Only when ingestion is authorized, follow [ingestion](ingest.md)** for this exact clipping — summarize
133	   into `wiki/sources/`, cross-reference, index, log. Ingestion requires authorization for this scope; reuse explicit session authorization. **If the clipping carries `fidelity: degraded`, do not quote its
134	   equations/symbols verbatim** — paraphrase them with attribution and verify every
135	   quoted span against the original PDF (guardrail #5). Note the fidelity ceiling
136	   on the resulting source page so a reader knows.
137	   - **`fidelity: tabular`** means the row pairings were reconstructed from layout.
138	     Cell *contents* are verbatim; which cell pairs with which is the reconstruction.
139	     Verify any code-to-text pairing against the PDF before a wiki page asserts it,
140	     and do not derive counts from it without checking.
141	   - **`fidelity: ocr`** means the text was recognised from page images. Words can be
142	     wrong without looking wrong; verify every quoted span, number and identifier
143	     (an ISBN, a table value) against the page image before a wiki page asserts it.
144	   - **`extraction: table-flattened`** means the rows were **lost** and could not be
145	     recovered on this machine. Do not assert any pairing from such a clipping;
146	     install the Xpdf tools and re-clip instead.
147	
148	## Preserving figures (`--figures`)
149	
150	Text extraction loses every figure, and in a PDF a graph is usually **vector
151	drawing**, not an embedded image, so `pdfimages` alone misses it. `--figures`
152	therefore renders **whole pages** with `pdftoppm -r 200 -png` and stores them in the
153	vault's figure convention.
154	
155	```bash
156	node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/clip-pdf.mjs" "<file.pdf>" --source="<url>" --figures            # auto
157	node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/clip-pdf.mjs" "<file.pdf>" --figures=all | --figures=3,5-7 --figures-max=60
158	# figures for a clipping that already exists, from a PDF you supply:
159	node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/clip-pdf.mjs" "<file.pdf>" --figures-only --clipping raw/clippings/<name>.md
160	```
161	
162	- **Pages chosen.** `auto` (the bare-flag default) selects a page when either holds:
163	  1. **Raster:** `pdfimages -list` shows an `image` row (not `smask`/`mask`) at least
164	     100x100 px and 0.75 in on the page, not a logo object repeated on half the pages.
165	  2. **Vector:** `pdftocairo -svg` shows at least 30 drawing elements outside glyph
166	     definitions AND the page is text-light (no text layer, or under 80 % of the
167	     document's median non-space characters per page), or at least 600 drawing
168	     elements regardless of text. A document whose text is outlined (no text layer
169	     at all) selects every drawn page. Raster pages skip the slower SVG probe.
170	
171	  It is deterministic and approximate: box-and-arrow diagrams on text pages are
172	  caught by the 30-element floor, but a ruled table can be a false positive and a
173	  figure drawn with very few strokes can be missed. Use `--figures=all` or a page
174	  list when the choice matters. `all` renders every page; a list renders exactly those.
175	- **Cap.** At most 40 pages per run (`--figures-max=N` to raise); a truncation is
176	  reported. Pages are not cropped: sidecars say `crop: full`.
177	- **Output.** `raw/figures/<clipping-slug>-p<N>.png` plus `<same>.md` with frontmatter
178	  `source`, `page`, `crop: full`, `dpi: 200`, `sha256`, `captured`,
179	  `clipping: "[[raw/clippings/<file>.md]]"`, `ai-generated: false`, then `# Title, page N`
180	  and a one-line machine description naming the candidates detected (`raster`,
181	  `vector`, or "none detected" for a page chosen by request).
182	- **Clipping frontmatter.** `figures: ["raw/figures/<slug>-p3.md", ...]` is added to the
183	  clipping's FRONTMATTER, after `source-hash`. The body is never edited. Only this tool
184	  writes it; it is pipeline state like `fidelity`.
185	- **Idempotent.** A page whose PNG hash already matches is left alone; a PNG identical
186	  to any existing figure is skipped as a duplicate; a sidecar with `crop` other than
187	  `full` (a hand-cropped figure) is never overwritten.
188	- **`--figures-only`** needs `--clipping <path>` (vault-relative, absolute or relative).
189	  It checks the PDF first: `source-hash` hashes the clipping's extracted text, so the
190	  PDF is re-extracted the way the clipping was and the hashes compared. A mismatch is
191	  refused (`--allow-pdf-mismatch` overrides); a clipping with no `source-hash` or one
192	  made by OCR cannot be checked and only warns.
193	- **Tools.** poppler `pdftoppm` (required), `pdfimages`, `pdftocairo`, `pdfinfo`; found
194	  on PATH or in the winget poppler folder. Missing tools never fail the clip: the run
195	  prints what is missing and how to install it (`--doctor` lists it), and `auto`
196	  degrades to whichever probe is available.
197	- **Operation bracket.** Figure PNG/sidecars and the clipping's frontmatter edit are
198	  ordinary vault writes inside the same `op-begin`/`op-commit` as the clip; op-commit
199	  commits whatever became dirty, so nothing extra is needed. `health.mjs` treats
200	  `raw/figures/` as assets, not clippings, so they never count toward the ingest backlog
201	  or as missing a `source-hash`.
202	- A render is a faithful page, not an interpretation. Describe what a figure shows only
203	  from looking at it (see [ingestion](ingest.md)).
204	
205	## Overriding the reading mode
206	
207	The detector is a heuristic and can misclassify **margin annotations beside a
208	body column** as a table. Aligned mode can splice a margin note into the adjacent
209	body line and leave hyphenated breaks unjoined. The result may read as ordinary
210	prose with only a `fidelity: tabular` caveat while no longer being quotable. **Assume neither mode is
211	right until you have looked at the output.**
212	
213	```bash
214	node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/clip-pdf.mjs" "<file.pdf>" --mode=reading-order --source="<url>"
215	```
216	
217	- `auto` (default) — the detector chooses.
218	- `reading-order` — force reading-order. Correct for prose, two-column papers, and
219	  body+margin layouts. Joins hyphenated line breaks; reads each column whole.
220	- `table` — force aligned reading. Correct for a real table. Always floors fidelity
221	  at `tabular`, because aligned output is reconstructed from horizontal position
222	  however you arrived at it.
223	
224	An override that **diverges** from the detector is recorded, not silent: the
225	clipping is stamped `extraction: reading-order-forced` and the run warns on stderr.
226	An override that agrees with the detector is a no-op and is not annotated. An
227	unknown `--mode=` value is an error, and `--mode=table` on a pdftotext without
228	`-table` is refused rather than quietly downgraded — believing you forced a mode
229	that was not applied is the failure this whole module exists to prevent.
230	
231	**How to tell which mode a document wants** — extract two pages both ways and look:
232	
233	```bash
234	pdftotext -enc UTF-8 -f 40 -l 41 "<file.pdf>" -            # reading-order
235	pdftotext -enc UTF-8 -f 40 -l 41 -table "<file.pdf>" -     # aligned
236	```
237	
238	If aligned mode puts *unrelated* text on the same line, it is a two-column or
239	margin layout — use `reading-order`. If reading-order emits a whole key column
240	followed by a whole value column, it is a table — use `table`.
241	
242	## Guardrails
243	
244	- **Never edit the body of anything under `raw/`** — clipped text is immutable
245	  source-of-truth (guardrail #1). Frontmatter is pipeline state, tooling-only
246	  (`fidelity`, `figures`).
247	- Figures are rendered pages, never crops or redrawings; do not hand-edit `raw/figures/`.
248	- `clip-pdf.mjs` is the **sole writer** to `raw/` for PDFs — the model never writes
249	  the clipping by hand (that would bypass dedup, decline, and hashing).
250	- **Fidelity, not truth**: a faithful extraction of a wrong paper is still wrong;
251	  `pdftotext` can also mangle multi-column layouts — verify quotes against the PDF
252	  before they land on a wiki page (guardrail #5).
253	
254	## Completion
255	
256	For a standalone clip, open an operation before the clipping helper writes, verify
257	its returned paths and extraction diagnostics, log once, commit, push and verify
258	remote publication through the shared operations contract. During discovery,
259	use the enclosing operation and report the results to its owner for completion.
260	Pass `--since <saved-token>` to the clipping helper so every written path enters
261	that operation's ledger. Capture-only requests end after this completion and
262	create no derived source or concept pages.
263	Capturing evidence does not by itself authorize ingestion; reuse explicit
264	discover-and-ingest authorization when it is already present.
265

- **Fidelity flag.** Math/symbol fonts (especially in older PDFs) extract lossily —
  `−`→`?`, `‖`→`jj`, superscripts flatten. This **cannot** be fixed without OCR, so
  it is *flagged*: when mangling is detected, the frontmatter gets
  **`fidelity: degraded`**. Clean captures omit the field. The full set of values a
  clipping can carry is: *(absent)* = high, **`tabular`** = rows reconstructed from
  layout, **`ocr`** = the text was recognised from page images, **`degraded`** = do
  not trust verbatim spans. Precedence is `degraded` over `ocr` over `tabular`: wrong
  characters are the worse defect, and recognised text with plausible characters is
  worse than a reconstructed pairing because nothing in the characters can show what
  the engine got wrong.
- **An OCR clipping never claims plain `high` fidelity.** Recognition errors produce
  well-formed words (`hrst` for `first`), so no check on the text can find them; the
  clipper declares the floor instead, `extraction: ocr` + **`fidelity: ocr`**, whether
  OCR was forced with `--ocr` or ran as the automatic fallback. A clean OCR pass is
  stamped the same as a poor one: the value says *unverified*, not *bad*. Clippings
  made before the floor existed carry `extraction: ocr` and no grade;
  `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/refresh-fidelity.mjs" --ocr-floor` lists them
  (dry run) and, with `--apply`, sets the floor. `refresh-fidelity.mjs` never clears an OCR flag, because
  re-reading the characters would call it healthy.
- **A text layer that drops or shifts letters is `degraded`.** A broken font map can leave only valid letters: some vanish, the whole alphabet shifts, or one letter stands for another. No other check sees it, because the characters are all letters. No Latin-script text lacks an `a` or a `t`, in any language, so a text of at least 5,000 letters whose share of one of fourteen common letters is far below every language's share is stamped `degraded` and sent to OCR. A shorter text, and a text that is not mostly Latin script, are not judged. Clippings made before this check are not re-graded for you: `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/refresh-fidelity.mjs" --inventory` lists the unmarked ones that now look broken, and only lists.
- **Re-assessment cannot clear a table flag.** `refresh-fidelity.mjs` re-derives
  fidelity from the stored text and drops flags that no longer hold, but a
  table-derived flag has no basis in the characters (a flattened table reads as
  clean prose), so clippings carrying `extraction: table-aware` or `table-flattened`
  are preserved rather than cleared.

## Steps

1. **Preflight** (once): `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/clip-pdf.mjs" --doctor`. It probes every
   external tool and prints what each missing one costs you; it is silent-and-OK only
   when all four are present. The clipper also prints this banner on **every** run
   when something is missing, so a degraded toolchain cannot go unnoticed. A missing
   `pdftotext` is fatal and the clipper exits — do not fabricate content. The rest are
   degradations: no `-table` loses table row pairings, and no `pdftoppm`/`tesseract`
   means scanned PDFs cannot be read at all.
2. **Clip** (this is the only writer to `raw/`):
   `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/clip-pdf.mjs" "<path/to/file.pdf>" --source="<canonical-url-if-any>" --quality=<tier> --topic="<topic>"`
   - `--source` is the citable origin (the paper's DOI/URL). Omit for a purely
     local PDF and the file path is recorded as the source.
   - **`--topic` whenever this clip belongs to a research run** — pass the topic
     string researcher discovery was given, identical across every clip in the run.
     It is what lets maintainer triage group the run's leftovers together. **Topic is
     recorded going forward only: there is no tool that can retro-fit it**, so a
     clip made without it is an *Unattributed* triage row permanently. Omit it
     only for a one-off clip with no research run behind it — an invented topic
     is worse than none, because it files the row under a heading the user has
     already worked through.
   - `--figures[=auto|all|3,5-7]` also renders figure pages (see **Preserving figures**).
     Pass it whenever the PDF's value is in graphs, diagrams or photos.
   - `--mode=auto|reading-order|table` overrides the reading-mode detector for a
     document it gets wrong. See **Overriding the reading mode** below.
   - A `thin` result means the PDF is scanned/encrypted and OCR also failed — a
     decline is recorded. An `ocr-unavailable` result means the OCR toolchain is
     missing, so **nothing was learned about the PDF** — no decline is recorded;
     install the tools and re-clip. Never invent the text either way.
3. **Verify** the clipping landed: read `raw/clippings/<slug>.md` and sanity-check
   that the extracted text is real prose, not garbled ligatures. `pdftotext`
   output is plain text — light and lossy on tables/figures.
4. **Only when ingestion is authorized, follow [ingestion](ingest.md)** for this exact clipping — summarize
   into `wiki/sources/`, cross-reference, index, log. Ingestion requires authorization for this scope; reuse explicit session authorization. **If the clipping carries `fidelity: degraded`, do not quote its
   equations/symbols verbatim** — paraphrase them with attribution and verify every
   quoted span against the original PDF (guardrail #5). Note the fidelity ceiling
   on the resulting source page so a reader knows.
   - **`fidelity: tabular`** means the row pairings were reconstructed from layout.
     Cell *contents* are verbatim; which cell pairs with which is the reconstruction.
     Verify any code-to-text pairing against the PDF before a wiki page asserts it,
     and do not derive counts from it without checking.
   - **`fidelity: ocr`** means the text was recognised from page images. Words can be
     wrong without looking wrong; verify every quoted span, number and identifier
     (an ISBN, a table value) against the page image before a wiki page asserts it.
   - **`extraction: table-flattened`** means the rows were **lost** and could not be
     recovered on this machine. Do not assert any pairing from such a clipping;
     install the Xpdf tools and re-clip instead.

## Preserving figures (`--figures`)

Text extraction loses every figure, and in a PDF a graph is usually **vector
drawing**, not an embedded image, so `pdfimages` alone misses it. `--figures`
therefore renders **whole pages** with `pdftoppm -r 200 -png` and stores them in the
vault's figure convention.

```bash
node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/clip-pdf.mjs" "<file.pdf>" --source="<url>" --figures            # auto
node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/clip-pdf.mjs" "<file.pdf>" --figures=all | --figures=3,5-7 --figures-max=60
# figures for a clipping that already exists, from a PDF you supply:
node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/clip-pdf.mjs" "<file.pdf>" --figures-only --clipping raw/clippings/<name>.md
```

- **Pages chosen.** `auto` (the bare-flag default) selects a page when either holds:
  1. **Raster:** `pdfimages -list` shows an `image` row (not `smask`/`mask`) at least
     100x100 px and 0.75 in on the page, not a logo object repeated on half the pages.
  2. **Vector:** `pdftocairo -svg` shows at least 30 drawing elements outside glyph
     definitions AND the page is text-light (no text layer, or under 80 % of the
     document's median non-space characters per page), or at least 600 drawing
     elements regardless of text. A document whose text is outlined (no text layer
     at all) selects every drawn page. Raster pages skip the slower SVG probe.

  It is deterministic and approximate: box-and-arrow diagrams on text pages are
  caught by the 30-element floor, but a ruled table can be a false positive and a
  figure drawn with very few strokes can be missed. Use `--figures=all` or a page
  list when the choice matters. `all` renders every page; a list renders exactly those.
- **Cap.** At most 40 pages per run (`--figures-max=N` to raise); a truncation is
  reported. Pages are not cropped: sidecars say `crop: full`.
- **Output.** `raw/figures/<clipping-slug>-p<N>.png` plus `<same>.md` with frontmatter
  `source`, `page`, `crop: full`, `dpi: 200`, `sha256`, `captured`,
  `clipping: "[[raw/clippings/<file>.md]]"`, `ai-generated: false`, then `# Title, page N`
  and a one-line machine description naming the candidates detected (`raster`,
  `vector`, or "none detected" for a page chosen by request).
- **Clipping frontmatter.** `figures: ["raw/figures/<slug>-p3.md", ...]` is added to the
  clipping's FRONTMATTER, after `source-hash`. The body is never edited. Only this tool
  writes it; it is pipeline state like `fidelity`.
- **Idempotent.** A page whose PNG hash already matches is left alone; a PNG identical
  to any existing figure is skipped as a duplicate; a sidecar with `crop` other than
  `full` (a hand-cropped figure) is never overwritten.
- **`--figures-only`** needs `--clipping <path>` (vault-relative, absolute or relative).
  It checks the PDF first: `source-hash` hashes the clipping's extracted text, so the
  PDF is re-extracted the way the clipping was and the hashes compared. A mismatch is
  refused (`--allow-pdf-mismatch` overrides); a clipping with no `source-hash` or one
  made by OCR cannot be checked and only warns.
- **Tools.** poppler `pdftoppm` (required), `pdfimages`, `pdftocairo`, `pdfinfo`; found
  on PATH or in the winget poppler folder. Missing tools never fail the clip: the run
  prints what is missing and how to install it (`--doctor` lists it), and `auto`
  degrades to whichever probe is available.
- **Operation bracket.** Figure PNG/sidecars and the clipping's frontmatter edit are
  ordinary vault writes inside the same `op-begin`/`op-commit` as the clip; op-commit
  commits whatever became dirty, so nothing extra is needed. `health.mjs` treats
  `raw/figures/` as assets, not clippings, so they never count toward the ingest backlog
  or as missing a `source-hash`.
- A render is a faithful page, not an interpretation. Describe what a figure shows only
  from looking at it (see [ingestion](ingest.md)).

## Overriding the reading mode

The detector is a heuristic and can misclassify **margin annotations beside a
body column** as a table. Aligned mode can splice a margin note into the adjacent
body line and leave hyphenated breaks unjoined. The result may read as ordinary
prose with only a `fidelity: tabular` caveat while no longer being quotable. **Assume neither mode is
right until you have looked at the output.**

```bash
node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/clip-pdf.mjs" "<file.pdf>" --mode=reading-order --source="<url>"
```

- `auto` (default) — the detector chooses.
- `reading-order` — force reading-order. Correct for prose, two-column papers, and
  body+margin layouts. Joins hyphenated line breaks; reads each column whole.
- `table` — force aligned reading. Correct for a real table. Always floors fidelity
  at `tabular`, because aligned output is reconstructed from horizontal position
  however you arrived at it.

An override that **diverges** from the detector is recorded, not silent: the
clipping is stamped `extraction: reading-order-forced` and the run warns on stderr.
An override that agrees with the detector is a no-op and is not annotated. An
unknown `--mode=` value is an error, and `--mode=table` on a pdftotext without
`-table` is refused rather than quietly downgraded — believing you forced a mode
that was not applied is the failure this whole module exists to prevent.

**How to tell which mode a document wants** — extract two pages both ways and look:

```bash
pdftotext -enc UTF-8 -f 40 -l 41 "<file.pdf>" -            # reading-order
pdftotext -enc UTF-8 -f 40 -l 41 -table "<file.pdf>" -     # aligned
```

If aligned mode puts *unrelated* text on the same line, it is a two-column or
margin layout — use `reading-order`. If reading-order emits a whole key column
followed by a whole value column, it is a table — use `table`.

## Guardrails

- **Never edit the body of anything under `raw/`** — clipped text is immutable
  source-of-truth (guardrail #1). Frontmatter is pipeline state, tooling-only
  (`fidelity`, `figures`).
- Figures are rendered pages, never crops or redrawings; do not hand-edit `raw/figures/`.
- `clip-pdf.mjs` is the **sole writer** to `raw/` for PDFs — the model never writes
  the clipping by hand (that would bypass dedup, decline, and hashing).
- **Fidelity, not truth**: a faithful extraction of a wrong paper is still wrong;
  `pdftotext` can also mangle multi-column layouts — verify quotes against the PDF
  before they land on a wiki page (guardrail #5).

## Completion

For a standalone clip, open an operation before the clipping helper writes, verify
its returned paths and extraction diagnostics, log once, commit, push and verify
remote publication through the shared operations contract. During discovery,
use the enclosing operation and report the results to its owner for completion.
Pass `--since <saved-token>` to the clipping helper so every written path enters
that operation's ledger. Capture-only requests end after this completion and
create no derived source or concept pages.
Capturing evidence does not by itself authorize ingestion; reuse explicit
discover-and-ingest authorization when it is already present.
